title: Java Interop Null-Safety Gaps Leading to Panic
platform_conditions: Kotlin/JVM language semantics; applies wherever Kotlin compiles to JVM bytecode (server JVM and Android runtime both)
security_mechanism: Kotlin's null safety is a compile-time type system, and every value coming from Java code arrives as a platform type (String!), a type the compiler neither null-checks nor forbids dereferencing. The null-safety invariant is therefore only as good as the assumption the Kotlin call site asserts: '!!' compiles to an intrinsic that throws KotlinNullPointerException at runtime when the Java callee returned null, and assigning a platform type to a non-null Kotlin variable throws an implicit NullPointerException later at the first use. On request-reachable paths this turns one unexpected Java return value into a guaranteed crash rather than a rejected input; lateinit val reads behave the same way, throwing UninitializedPropertyAccessException when initialization was skipped.

source_sink_clues.source: Any Java-side value crossing into Kotlin: return values of Java methods fed by request data, Java framework callbacks, deserialized Java objects whose fields the attacker controls to be null.
source_sink_clues.sink: '!!' non-null assertions on platform types, implicit assignment of platform types to non-null Kotlin types, and lateinit property reads on attacker-influenced paths

tracking_guards: Check the call site handles the platform type explicitly: elvis with a safe fallback ('?: return null' / '?: throw'), safe-call chains ('?.'), or a requireNotNull(...) check with a handled failure before any further use; verify lateinit properties have an ::isInitialized guard or are replaced by nullable types on input-driven paths.
not_candidate_when: The Java callee is contractually non-null and locally verified (returns a freshly constructed object, never null), the assertion sits on a value the server itself produced rather than on request data, or the failure is handled (elvis/requireNotNull) and cannot crash a shared process on a request path.
public_references: Kotlin documentation: calling Java from Kotlin and platform types — https://kotlinlang.org/docs/java-interop.html
